record.summary: Policy of Paraguay's Supreme Court of Justice guiding magistrates and judicial staff on the ethical, responsible and transparent use of AI systems, including in-house, acquired and licensed systems. Under a principle of human oversight it lists permitted supporting uses and forbids delegating decisions to AI, fully automating processes that affect fundamental rights, using AI to determine guilt or innocence, and setting penalties without human intervention. Parties must be told when AI is used, generative-AI text must be disclosed and prompts documented, and wholly opaque systems are banned. Further rules cover non-discrimination, data protection and security, and AI literacy training.

changes.summary: Annex Art. 8(d)-(e) read more closely: AI may not be used to determine guilt or innocence, and penalties may not be set without human intervention (version 1: 'using AI to determine guilt or set penalties'); Art. 11 bans systems whose working is 'completamente opaco', now 'wholly opaque'

judgment.status_reasoning: Resolution No. 12.677 of 4 Mar 2026 approves the policy (Art. 1) and authorises its application (Art. 3), with no later commencement date; Art. 4 has a working group report periodically on implementation. No stored file shows an amendment, a Version 2 or a repeal, so 'In force' stands as of 18 Oct 2026. The policy binds magistrates and staff of the Judiciary (Annex Art. 4) and contains prohibitions (Annex Arts. 8, 11, 14, 17), so legal force 'Binding'.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published and date_in_force 2026-03-04: the resolution is dated 4 Mar 2026 ('Resolución Nq 12.677, de fecha 4 de marzo de 2026'; annex headed 'Asunción, 4 de marzo de 2026'), and Art. 3 authorises application without a separate date.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Rules the Supreme Court sets for AI use across the whole Judiciary, all courts and judicial circumscriptions, including duties towards the parties (disclosure, no AI determination of guilt). That is a government body's rules for a whole branch and its proceedings, like a government's rules for public-sector AI use, not one institution's own policy in the sense of the 15 Oct 2026 precedent; in scope with no note.
